A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Llamdex and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Content can be reliably matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original accuracy, efficiency, privacy-budget, and ablation results in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds membership-inference and inaccurate-schema evaluations.

M1.justification: The frozen LLM/expert architecture, encoder token mapping, decoder, synthetic connector training, optional DP expert training, and iterative reasoning procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The same five datasets remain, including adult in Appendix C. v4 adds Titanic scenarios involving membership inference and inaccurate schema ranges. Purchase-100 identifies the attack's competition provenance, not an additional evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: DP-OPT disappears from all four privacy-comparison panels in Figure 4, although its baseline description and Appendix E.5 remain. Other customization comparators are retained; MICO is introduced as an attacker.

E3.justification: v4 adds membership-inference testing across privacy budgets, specifying attack AUC and TPR at 10% FPR. Appendix D.5 adds fixed-data tests with declared age ranges [0,40], [0,100], [0,1000], and [0,5000], evaluated using AUC-ROC. Existing Section 6.1 settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Two focused robustness analyses are added: MICO attacks against Titanic expert models and sensitivity to inaccurate age ranges. The expert-weight and insertion-layer ablations in v4 Section 6.5 already appeared in v3 Appendix D.1–D.2.

E5.justification: Both versions specify mean accuracy over five independent runs and show error bars in Figure 4. No changed run counts, seed disclosures, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests are documented.

E6.justification: v4 removes DP-OPT's Figure 4 results and adds Figure 5 and Table 12. The latter reports AUC-ROC values 0.7940, 0.8103, 0.8141, and 0.8119 for the four age ranges. Tables 1–11 retain their values. The new attack results are internally inconsistent: Section 6.4 states accuracy 0.757 at epsilon 1, whereas Figure 5 plots approximately 0.50.

T1.justification: The differential-privacy definition, formal problem assumptions, optimization objective, and token-mapping equations are unchanged. The added empirical metrics introduce no new mathematical derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same model-based customization claims, including improvements up to 14% over LoRA and 26% over private synthesis methods. The new experiments provide additional supporting material without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: v4 newly interprets the attack experiment as strong privacy protection with minimal utility loss, although its text and figure disagree. Appendix D.5 attributes schema-range robustness to using broad semantic estimates. Existing limitations concerning single-expert, tabular customization and DP tradeoffs remain.

D1.justification: The introduction adds a source-code availability statement and a Llamdex repository link absent from v3. Existing implementation, hardware, optimizer, and baseline hyperparameter descriptions are retained. The PDFs establish the new access information, not the repository's actual availability.

R1.justification: The new privacy discussion positions the evaluation against MICO, described as the SaTML 2023 Purchase-100 competition winner. This is a limited addition to research positioning; Section 3 and the bibliography remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Two appendix ablations move into a new Section 6.5, and the appendix organization is updated. Author/contact information changes, and acknowledgments and a conference notice are added. Most existing prose is preserved.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figure 5 and Table 12, redraws Figure 4 with DP-OPT removed and adjusted legends and axis limits, and relocates v3 Figures 5–6 as main-text Figures 6–7. The overall two-column layout and other displays are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The schema-robustness evidence and code-access information are useful additions, but the new privacy evidence is inconsistent: Section 6.4 reports accuracy 0.757 at epsilon 1 and non-private attack TPR 0.130, while Figure 5 plots about 0.50 and 0.106 respectively. DP-OPT's privacy-comparison results also disappear despite its retained description. These benefits and reporting problems prevent a reliable judgment of net improvement.
